raw.assessment: The incumbent demonstrates near-target workshop performance on repeated three-compartment orders (seven to nine minutes), while mixed batches contain every extreme delay. This supports investigating variant handling, but complexity and switching remain confounded and selection, insertion, checking and packing times are unseparated. Five customer reports indicate a completeness concern without establishing five verified omissions. Seven of ten observed customers succeeded unaided. A concrete limitation is D2-O5: overlapping widths among first-attempt and retried partitions weaken a simple width-only explanation; they neither exclude joint fit problems nor establish their cause. No supplied observation demonstrates all pilot targets together.

openings.claim: Changing order variants may add selection and checking delays; grouping otherwise identical orders could reduce the incumbent's long completion times.
openings.delta: Test whether sequence contributes beyond the intrinsic work required by compartment count and color.
openings.prediction: With layout/color composition held constant, interleaved orders take longer specifically in selection or checking than grouped orders; similar insertion times would strengthen the switching account.
openings.probe: Use reusable samples within the 15-sample allowance. Have both workers perform matched grouped and interleaved sequences, counterbalancing sequence order and logging each phase and insertion retries. Retain accepted specifications; assess feasible scheduling against the fixed delivery date before adoption.
assumptions: Reused samples remain representative; record wear and practice effects.
Any scheduling benefit must survive actual order composition.

openings.claim: The generic layout diagram may leave the short partition's role unclear even when all correct parts are present.
openings.delta: Separate instruction ambiguity from physical incompleteness using independently audited kits.
openings.prediction: An ordered-layout diagram identifying every partition reduces short-partition questions and placement errors with complete, unchanged kits.
openings.probe: Randomly split ten participants between existing and order-specific diagrams using matched audited kits. Record unaided completion, short-partition errors and preparation time. Treat this small comparison as exploratory. Adopt only if combined initial spending stays within 500, added materials within 0.40 per order, and delivery remains feasible.
assumptions: Ordered diagrams accurately reflect supplied parts.
Partitions remain removable; footprint, capacity, compartment counts and exterior colors are unchanged.

raw.assessment: One interaction hypothesis is supported as worth probing, not established as effective. Missing-part reports and short-partition confusion suggest a shared packing-to-unpacking interface; insertion difficulty and stage-specific time remain unresolved.

openings.claim: Cross an order-specific completeness template with an order-specific placement guide through shared partition codes. Workers verify each required loose partition against a reusable bench template; the matching customer diagram maps those same codes to positions in the ordered arrangement. This may permit verified kit packing with less workshop assembly while retaining unaided customer success.
openings.delta: A completeness template alone cannot explain placement, and a placement guide alone cannot establish that the correct pieces were packed. Their named interface is the common order-and-partition code carried from the bench check to the customer diagram. The predicted interaction is fewer wrong-piece placement attempts and help requests when both mechanisms use the same mapping.
openings.prediction: For otherwise identical kits, the combined condition should reduce incorrect placements and requests for help more than either component alone, with an interaction beyond their separate effects. Total workshop time may fall if avoided insertion time exceeds template checking time; customer insertion difficulty could defeat the benefit.
openings.probe: Use 12 of the 15 sample sets for an exploratory 2-by-2 comparison: completeness template present/absent and matching placement guide present/absent, with each of the three compartment counts represented in every condition. Hold kit presentation and components constant. Time selection, insertion, checking and packing separately; independently audit contents and exterior color. Allocate ten participants to first-use trials across conditions and record ordered-layout success, wrong placements and help requests. Separately compare workshop totals with the assembled workflow. This small probe can reject the mechanism but cannot establish the 60-unit success rates.
assumptions: Required parts, dimensions, capacity, selected counts and exterior colors remain unchanged; all joints remain dismantlable.
Codes can remain visible without weakening parts or creating placement ambiguity.
Templates and replacement diagrams fit the 500 initial and 0.40 recurring limits, and preparation fits the fixed delivery date; verify these before adoption.
Customers can assemble the supplied joints without workshop insertion; observed second attempts do not establish their cause.

openings.claim: Variant switching may prolong selection/checking independently of layout complexity.
openings.discriminator: Grouped versus interleaved orders with identical layout/color composition; similar insertion times support switching.
openings.probe: Counterbalance both workers on reusable samples; time phases, log retries, wear and practice.
openings.uncertainty: Mixed batches confound switching with complexity; benefit must survive actual composition.

openings.claim: Order-specific diagrams may resolve short-partition ambiguity despite complete kits.
openings.discriminator: Fewer questions and placement errors with audited identical kits isolates instruction effects.
openings.probe: Randomly split ten participants between generic and ordered diagrams; record unaided completion, errors and preparation time.
openings.uncertainty: Exploratory; diagrams must match parts. Missing-part reports do not establish five verified omissions.

openings.claim: Shared partition codes connect completeness templates to placement guides, potentially enabling verified loose-kit packing.
openings.discriminator: Combined template/guide outperforms separate effects; saved insertion exceeds checking time.
openings.fit: Uncertain: costs, visible nonweakening codes and customer insertion feasibility.
openings.probe: Explore 2x2 template/guide conditions using 12 sets spanning all three counts; hold presentation/components fixed. Audit contents/color, time phases, assign ten first-use trials, record success/errors/help; separately compare assembled-workflow totals.
openings.uncertainty: Customer joint difficulty may defeat savings; overlapping widths do not establish retry causes.

lineage.reason: Distinct coded-interface interaction and assembly transfer.

post_distill.decision: Allocate exploratory probes within 15 samples and ten participants. Preserve 30x20 footprint, assortment, removable joints, ordered counts/colors and fixed delivery. Combined initial spend <=500; added materials <=0.40/order. No stipulated evidence establishes the 60-unit targets: >=98% complete, median <=8 minutes, >=90% unaided.
